structured.answer: It's savings that come off my salary. My employer puts in up to 7.5% and I put in up to 2.5%. After 6 years from the first deposit I can take all of it out with no tax, and before that I can but it's taxed and costs a lot. I'm keeping it because the boss's money is basically free and the page says it's "כמעט תמיד הצעד הראשון", but the example that's supposed to show it's better only beat an ordinary account by about 415 ₪, and that confused me.

stuck.why: The hishtalmut only wins by 415.84 ₪ after 10 years. I expected a much bigger gap. If it's only 415, why is it such a big deal?
Costs say 2,402.23 ₪ for the keren and 466.12 ₪ for the securities account. Written in shekels, that looks like a lot of fees and it scared me. I didn't get why the keren still comes out ahead.

stuck.where: Screen 2, paragraph about the employer's money
stuck.why: It says the employer's money 'מחוץ להשוואה'. Does that mean the free 7.5% isn't even in those bars? Then the real gap is bigger? I'm not sure I got that right.
There's a minus there. So with some funds I'd actually lose? That made me nervous about which company to pick.

findings.what: The main comparison shows only a 415 ₪ advantage. It makes the keren look barely worth it, while the free employer money is apparently left out of the comparison. That's the one thing that matters to me
Fees in shekels are 5x higher for the keren (2,402 vs 466). It looks bad and nothing nearby explains it
A negative number in the range (342.02-) with no explanation of when you lose
Lots of dotted-underline terms and codes (TXH-09, PF-06) on every row that I'd have to decode again and again
The fee is only written as 'עד 2% בשנה', a small percent, with no shekel figure next to it
The bar colours are only explained by the labels above each bar. OK, but I had to look back and forth
The 47% in the warning is scary but it's not clear on what
